name: Trainy

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Konduktor is BYOC: custom platform fee plus per-node pricing, with the customer's cloud hardware bill separate. A legacy/current docs statement says on-demand users are billed compute only while a workload is ACTIVE, but no rates are published and the former /on-demand page now returns 404.

plans.name: Pluto Free Hosted
plans.note: Experiment tracking only: up to 2 seats and 2 GB storage; not GPU compute.

plans.name: Pluto Pro Hosted
plans.note: Experiment tracking only. $250 per seat/month, up to 10 seats; 10B data points/month, 10 TB storage, unlimited tracked hours and run forking.

plans.name: Pluto Enterprise
plans.note: Experiment tracking only: more than 10 seats, custom storage/data limits, SSO, audit logs, single-tenant or on-prem, support/SLA.

caveats: Pricing FAQ explicitly says Trainy is not a cloud provider. Platform plus per-node quote on own cloud; Pluto $250/seat/month is experiment tracking, NOT GPU rental. YC startup discount 50% Konduktor 6mo (or free under 5 nodes); hardware remains own-cloud cost.
Inventory exclusion: BYOC GPU management, explicitly not cloud provider. Card contains no numeric compute modes and no selectable price plan.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Discount: current-batch YC companies get 50% off Konduktor for 6 months (or free under 5 nodes), one year of free Pluto hosted Pro, and one free performance-tuning consultation; hardware/cloud spend is not included.

fleet.notes: Konduktor BYOC uses custom cluster-sized quote; on-demand GPU page routes to demo/team contact. Customer-cloud quotas or negotiated capacity determine fleet, not a public signup allowance.

snapshot_auto.quote: When a Konduktor job runs, its containers execute in **ephemeral pods**. Local storage (`/tmp`, `/root`, or your `workdir`) is ephemeral and wiped when the pod restarts or completes.
snapshot_auto.note: Batch-job scheduler on Kubernetes; state survives only via your own writes to S3/GCS (docs show app-level training-checkpoint resume using RESTART_ATTEMPT).

secret_proxy.quote: Konduktor mounts your cloud credentials into the job containers and places them in `~/.aws` (S3) or `~/.config/gcloud` (GS) at startup.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are Kubernetes secrets exposed as env vars (konduktor secret create --kind env), mounted files (/konduktor/default-secrets) or git-ssh keys (GIT_SSH_COMMAND with key path); no injecting proxy.

isolation.quote: When a Konduktor job runs, its containers execute in **ephemeral pods**.
isolation.note: Konduktor schedules ordinary Kubernetes pods/containers on the customer's own cluster; shared-kernel container isolation, not a VM/microVM.

image_oci.quote: Containers must be Debian/Ubuntu based and use `apt` as a package manager ... permit login/run as `root`
image_oci.note: Jobs specify a container image_id; user-supplied Docker/OCI images are run.

docker_inside.note: not offered: no documentation of running Docker/nested containers inside a Konduktor job pod; jobs are plain unprivileged Kubernetes pods.

nested_virt.quote: Containers must be Debian/Ubuntu based and use `apt` as a package manager
nested_virt.note: not offered: no mention of /dev/kvm or nested virtualization; standard Kubernetes GPU pods.

egress_ip_type.note: derived: BYOC deploys into the customer's own cloud VPC/datacenter network, so egress is whatever datacenter IP type that cloud account provides.

snapshot.quote: Local storage (`/tmp`, `/root`, or your `workdir`) is ephemeral and wiped when the pod restarts or completes. Therefore, we recommend uploading to cloud storage any data that must survive restarts.
snapshot.note: No provider-managed disk/memory snapshot; only app-level checkpoint files the user writes to S3/GCS.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Local storage (`/tmp`, `/root`, or your `workdir`) is ephemeral and wiped when the pod restarts or completes.
snapshot_on_demand.note: not offered: no snapshot/checkpoint API; only manual object-storage uploads.

fork.quote: Konduktor (GPU cluster scheduling and orchestration on Kubernetes). Batch jobs, Kueue priority queueing with preemption, automatic restarts onto healthy nodes...
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (batch job scheduler, not machine cloning); Pluto's 'run forking' is experiment-tracking lineage, not a compute-machine clone.

fork_running.quote: Konduktor (GPU cluster scheduling and orchestration on Kubernetes).
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

pause_resume.quote: SUSPENDED (by user): The workload was manually stopped by a user using `konduktor stop <JOB_ID>`. It can be unsuspended with `konduktor start <JOB_ID>`.
pause_resume.note: Jobs can be manually stopped and restarted via CLI.

persistent_disk.quote: When a Konduktor job runs, its containers execute in ephemeral pods. Local storage (/tmp, /root, or your workdir) is ephemeral and wiped when the pod restarts or completes. Therefore, we recommend uploading to cloud storage any data that must survive restarts or be analyzed later.
persistent_disk.note: Not a contradiction: Konduktor's 'suspend/start' (konduktor stop / konduktor start) is a scheduler-queue pause (job goes to SUSPENDED and is later rescheduled onto a fresh pod), not a filesystem-preserving pause/resume. Docs explicitly recommend app-level checkpointing to S3/GCS (RESTART_ATTEMPT env var) because local disk does not survive a restart. No PersistentVolume/PVC or disk snapshot feature is documented anywhere in the docs (checked llms-full.txt for 'persistent volume', 'PVC', 'snapshot' with no relevant hits). Card's persistent_disk=false is correct as-is.

volume_attach.quote: Runtime sync works through direct writes to your configured object store (S3, GCS, etc.) rather than automatic file syncing.
volume_attach.note: No documented persistent-volume attach feature; only object-storage bucket sync is offered.

volume_shared.quote: by default each machine auto-creates its own `konduktor-filemounts-<username>-<user_hash>` bucket. Admins can instead point every engineer at a single shared bucket
volume_shared.note: Sharing is via an object-storage bucket configured by users/admins, not a shared block volume mounted live by multiple running machines.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Konduktor (GPU cluster scheduling and orchestration on Kubernetes). Batch jobs, Kueue priority queueing with preemption, automatic restarts onto healthy nodes...
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; it is a batch job scheduler, not a persistent idle sandbox with auto-stop.

live_resize.quote: resources: cpus: 1 # number of cpu cores memory: 10 # memory request in GiB (int)
live_resize.note: not offered: no documented API to change a running job's CPU/RAM without recreating it.

agent_harnesses.quote: AI-Assisted Workflows: Install the [Konduktor Skills](https://github.com/Trainy-ai/konduktor-skills) plugin to get AI help drafting task YAMLs, writing Python SDK code, and constructing CLI commands directly in your editor.
agent_harnesses.note: Konduktor Skills is an editor/CLI-authoring aid for the user's own coding assistant, not a preinstalled coding-agent template running inside the sandbox.

harness_api.quote: Konduktor and Pluto both expose MCP servers. Through Konduktor, an AI agent can launch workloads, read job and cluster logs, read GPU and system metrics, and restart jobs.
harness_api.note: MCP server controls the orchestration platform (launch/restart jobs, read logs/metrics); it is not an API that drives a coding harness running inside the sandbox.

own_agent_api.quote: Trainy builds GPU infrastructure for foundation-model and research teams.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no browser/computer-use/research task agent product)

lang_python.quote: Work with Konduktor programmatically from Python.
lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK/CLI (konduktor-nightly on PyPI) is the primary interface.

lang_node.quote: Work with Konduktor programmatically from Python.
lang_node.note: not offered: only a Python SDK/CLI is documented; no Node.js SDK or out-of-the-box Node runtime is mentioned.

egress_allowlist.quote: Deploys in your VPC: AWS, GCP, Azure, bare-metal, and more...
egress_allowlist.note: derived: BYOC deploys into the customer's own VPC, so outbound network restrictions would be configured via the customer's own cloud security groups, not a Trainy-specific feature.

egress_http_rules.quote: Deploys in your VPC: AWS, GCP, Azure, bare-metal, and more...
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no HTTP method/path-level egress rules documented; BYOC leaves network policy to the customer's own cloud.

guest_firewall.quote: When a Konduktor job runs, its containers execute in **ephemeral pods**.
guest_firewall.note: derived: isolation is shared-kernel Kubernetes containers, not a full VM/microVM with root=true, so in-guest nftables/iptables control is not assumed to be available.

static_egress_ip.quote: Deploys in your VPC: AWS, GCP, Azure, bare-metal, and more...
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no fixed outbound IP feature documented; BYOC networking follows the customer's own cloud setup.

windows.quote: Containers must be Debian/Ubuntu based and use `apt` as a package manager
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (Linux container images only)

macos.quote: Containers must be Debian/Ubuntu based and use `apt` as a package manager
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (Linux GPU container platform)

byoc.quote: Konduktor deploys into your own cloud (BYOC) with a platform fee plus per-node pricing that scales sub-linearly as your cluster grows.

eu_data_residency.quote: Deploys in your VPC: AWS, GCP, Azure, bare-metal, and more...
eu_data_residency.note: derived: BYOC deploys into whatever cloud account/region the customer chooses, so EU residency is achievable if the customer's own AWS/GCP/Azure account/region is in the EU.

max_session_h.note: Max run duration is a user-set Kueue label per job, not a fixed platform-imposed session cap; jobs otherwise run until completion/failure.

public_ipv4.quote: `trainy.us` endpoints use `https` while direct IP endpoints use `http`. ... Optionally, use `--direct` to display direct IP endpoints instead of `trainy.us` endpoints.
public_ipv4.note: Konduktor Serve exposes deployments via a direct IP endpoint (in addition to a trainy.us hostname); Konduktor deploys into the customer's own VPC (AWS/GCP/Azure/bare-metal), so the underlying IP is provisioned from that cloud, but Trainy's own tooling surfaces a direct/public IP for reaching services.

ingress_rules.quote: Konduktor Serve is a powerful feature that simplifies deploying and managing ML models and general applications on Kubernetes. ... Accessible at `<COMPANY>.trainy.us`
ingress_rules.note: Konduktor routes serving traffic through per-company trainy.us hostnames (vs. raw direct IP), and interactive SSH access is gated behind Tailscale ACLs/authkeys (docs.trainy.ai/tailscale.md) rather than open ports, i.e. the platform provides auth/hostname-scoped and allowlist-based access control to exposed services rather than raw open ports; underlying security-group rules are otherwise inherited from the customer's own cloud (BYOC).

arm64.quote: Konduktor GPU cluster scheduling & management ... Deploys in your VPC: AWS, GCP, Azure, bare-metal, and more...
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Konduktor is an NVIDIA GPU (H100, etc.) training/inference cluster scheduler for x86 Kubernetes nodes; no ARM64 CPU or GPU nodes are mentioned anywhere in docs, pricing, or blog content.

usage_api.quote: Konduktor is BYOC: custom platform fee plus per-node pricing, with the customer's cloud hardware bill separate. ... on-demand users are billed compute only while a workload is ACTIVE, but no rates are published and the former /on-demand page now returns 404.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; Trainy is not a cloud provider; it schedules jobs on customer's own AWS/GCP/Azure/bare-metal infrastructure. Billable compute usage (GPU-seconds, vCPU-seconds) is reported by the underlying cloud provider, not by Trainy. MCP server and CLI can read job logs and system metrics, but no billing/usage breakdown API is documented. Platform fee is via sales-custom quote.
